proof:
# A full positive cap circuit does not glue cap homotheties globally

This exact planar counterexample shows that whole-body BM equality
cannot be removed from
`candidate d99f14f216938f2e`
merely because every captured-side comparison in a through-interior
cover is an equality. Every endpoint cut below is proper. The three
normals form a minimal full-rank positive circuit, and the normalized
endpoint cap fractions are unequal in EVERY direction.

## 1. The bodies and their actual Minkowski midpoint

In cyclic counterclockwise order, set

    A=conv{(-1,2),(-2,-1),(2,-3),(2,-1)},
    B=conv{(-13/8,17/8),(-5/2,-1/2),(3/2,-5/2),(3/2,-1)}.

Equivalently,

    A={-3x+y<=5, -x-2y<=4, x<=2, x+y<=1},
    B={-3x+y<=7, -x-2y<=7/2, x<=3/2, x+y<=1/2}.

The four successive edge directions are the same, with strictly
positive edge lengths, for both polygons. Define

    K={-3x+y<=6, -x-2y<=15/4, x<=7/4, x+y<=3/4}.

Its cyclic vertices are

    (-21/16,33/16), (-9/4,-3/4), (7/4,-11/4), (7/4,-1).

The displayed inequalities give (A+B)/2 subset K. Each vertex of
K is the average of the correspondingly indexed vertices of A and
B, giving the reverse inclusion by convexity. Therefore

    K=(A+B)/2.                                       (1)

Every displayed inequality is strict at the origin. Thus 0 belongs
to the interior of all three bodies, in particular to int(K).

## 2. A minimal positive circuit and three different cap maps

Let

    H_1={x>=0}, H_2={y>=0}, H_3={-x-y>=0}.

Their normals sum to zero and span R^2. No pair has a positive
dependence, so this is a minimal positive circuit. They cover the
whole plane: a point with x<0 and y<0 belongs to H_3, while every
other point belongs to H_1 or H_2.

Write A_i=A intersect H_i and similarly B_i,K_i. The exact cap
homotheties are

    B_1=(3/4) A_1+(0,-1/4),
    B_2=(17/16) A_2+(-9/16,0),
    B_3=A_3+(-1/2,1/2).                              (2)

Each translation is tangent to its actual cut line, as required.
These identities can be checked directly from the inequalities:

* On H_1, the inequality -3x+y<=5 in A is redundant. The remaining
  cap is 0<=x<=2, -2-x/2<=y<=1-x. The first map in (2) changes
  these exactly to 0<=x<=3/2, -7/4-x/2<=y<=1/2-x, the B cap.
* On H_2, the A cap is the triangle y>=0,
  (y-5)/3<=x<=1-y. The second map changes it exactly to
  y>=0, (y-7)/3<=x<=1/2-y, the B cap.
* On H_3, x+y<=1 and x+y<=1/2 are redundant in A and B,
  respectively. Translation by (-1/2,1/2) preserves x+y and
  changes the other three right sides of A into those of B.

The corresponding midpoint maps are

    K_1=(7/8) A_1+(0,-1/8),
    K_2=(33/32) A_2+(-9/32,0),
    K_3=A_3+(-1/4,1/4).                              (3)

The same inequality substitutions, using K's displayed right sides,
prove (3) exactly. Since a convex set satisfies
(E+lambda E+v)/2=((1+lambda)/2)E+v/2, equations (2)--(3) prove

    K_i=(A_i+B_i)/2                                  (4)

as actual sets, for all three caps.

## 3. Exact areas and all three captured-side BM equalities

The full areas are

    |A|=10, |B|=271/32, |K|=1183/128.

The cap areas are

    i       |A_i|       |B_i|       |K_i|
    1         5         45/16      245/64
    2        8/3        289/96     363/128
    3       55/8        55/8       55/8.

Every entry is positive and strictly less than its corresponding
full-body area. Hence all six endpoint cuts, and all three source
cuts, are proper. Equations (2)--(3), or this table directly, give

    |K_i|^(1/2)=(|A_i|^(1/2)+|B_i|^(1/2))/2

for every i. The endpoint fractions are respectively

    i=1: 1/2 versus 90/271,
    i=2: 4/15 versus 289/813,
    i=3: 11/16 versus 220/271.

Each pair is unequal. Thus the additional unequal-fraction premise
from the prior simplex-rigidity note would not repair the proposed
deletion of its whole-body BM premise.

## 4. Global homothety and whole-body BM both fail

The edge of A from (-2,-1) to (2,-3) has vector (4,-2); the
corresponding B edge has the SAME vector. A positive global
homothety would therefore have ratio one. But A's vertical right
edge has vector (0,2), and B's corresponding edge has vector
(0,3/2), forcing ratio 3/4. These uniquely oriented edges must
correspond under any positive homothety. The contradiction proves
that A and B are not positively homothetic.

There is also an exact area certificate of strict whole-body BM.
Writing a=|A|, b=|B| and k=|K|, one has

    4k-a-b=37/2>0,
    (4k-a-b)^2-4ab=7/2>0.

It follows that 4k>a+b+2sqrt(ab), equivalently

    |K|^(1/2)>(|A|^(1/2)+|B|^(1/2))/2.              (5)

All three bodies are quadrilaterals. Thus neither the proposed
global homothety nor the resulting simplex classification holds.

## 5. Complete actual integer-fiber embedding

Form the compact convex body in R times R^2

    C=conv( ({-1} times A) union ({0} times K)
                                      union ({1} times B) ).

It is full dimensional and its integer projection is {-1,0,1}.
The endpoint fibers are A and B, while (1) makes the middle fiber
exactly K. In fact the middle set in the displayed convex hull is
already forced by the two endpoints. Hence no fibers are hypothetical
or enlarged in this embedding.

Use the three closed ambient halfspaces R times H_i. They cover
the entire ambient space, and their endpoint/source captured-side
BM comparisons are precisely the three exact equalities above.
The total mixed area is M=3547/128. The largest fiber area is
10<M/2, so even strict three-fiber noheavy holds.

No global critical-cap claim is made. In particular the three
ambient cap masses are not equal, and their budgets do not give an
OC obstruction. The example refutes exactly the proposed gluing
of captured-side equality maps under a proper through-point cover.

## 6. A full-dimensional counterexample in every d>=3

This counterexample can be lifted while retaining actual d-dimensional
positive homotheties of all caps; an ordinary Cartesian product would
not have this property when the three cap ratios differ.

Put m=d-2 and introduce t=(t_1,...,t_m). With the planar A,B,K above,
define the convex polytopes

    A^d={(x,y,t):(x,y) in A, t_j>=0,
                              sum_j t_j<=19-11x-y},
    B^d={(x,y,t):(x,y) in B, t_j>=0,
                              sum_j t_j<=14-11x-y},
    K^d={(x,y,t):(x,y) in K, t_j>=0,
                              sum_j t_j<=33/2-11x-y}.

All are bounded and full dimensional. The common point
(0,0,1/m,...,1/m) is interior to all three: their planar facet
inequalities are strict there, every t_j is positive, and its sum
one is strictly below all three roof values at the planar origin.
The three halfspaces H_i now ignore t. They still cover R^d, their
cuts are proper, and their boundaries contain that common interior
point. Their normals form a rank-two minimal positive circuit.

Let lambda_i,v_i be the ratios and translations in (2), and write
phi_A=19-11x-y, phi_B=14-11x-y, phi_K=33/2-11x-y.
Direct substitution gives

    phi_B(lambda_i(x,y)+v_i)=lambda_i phi_A(x,y),
    phi_K(((1+lambda_i)/2)(x,y)+v_i/2)
                           =((1+lambda_i)/2)phi_A(x,y).

Therefore extending the cap maps (2) by t -> lambda_i t, and the
midpoint maps (3) by t -> ((1+lambda_i)/2)t, proves

    B^d intersect H_i
       =lambda_i(A^d intersect H_i)+(v_i,0),
    K^d intersect H_i
       =( (A^d intersect H_i)+(B^d intersect H_i) )/2.

The direct midpoint inclusion (A^d+B^d)/2 subset K^d follows from
the planar inclusion and the affine roof equations. Conversely the
cap identities and their cover imply K^d subset (A^d+B^d)/2. Thus
K^d is the ACTUAL full-dimensional Minkowski midpoint, and every
captured-side d-dimensional BM comparison is exactly tight.

The lifted bodies are not globally homothetic. Their planar projections
are the original polygons cut by their nonnegative-roof inequalities,
with cyclic vertices

    proj A^d: (-1,2),(-2,-1),(2,-3),(9/5,-4/5),
    proj B^d: (-13/8,17/8),(-5/2,-1/2),(3/2,-5/2),(27/20,-17/20).

Their bottom edge vectors remain equal to (4,-2), while the next
edge vectors are (-1/5,11/5) and (-3/20,33/20), with ratio 3/4.
Thus these projections are not positively homothetic, precluding a
positive homothety of the lifted bodies. Whole-body BM is strict by
its classical equality characterization.

Placing A^d,K^d,B^d at integer bases -1,0,1 gives the same exact
actual-fiber embedding as Section 5 in every d>=3. The extra planar
claims about numerical fractions and strict noheavy in Sections 3
and 5 are not asserted for these higher-dimensional lifts without
their separate volume calculation. The all-dimensional conclusion
here is the verified failure of global homothety under the stated
proper captured-side equality cover.
